# 5 of Our Favorite Parenting Apps

- [PANW](https://www.portlandpediatric.com/author/pnwstaging/)
- [February 28, 2023](https://www.portlandpediatric.com/2023/02/28/)
- 9:00 am

![parent looking at apps on phone](https://www.portlandpediatric.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/man-looking-at-apps-on-phone.jpg)

There are only so many apps one can use regularly, and there are thousands of parenting apps to choose from. So how does a parent or guardian decide which parenting apps are worth installing and which aren’t?

## **Pediatrician Approved: Top Parenting App**

Your pediatrician is a great place to start. The next time you head in for a [newborn](https://www.portlandpediatric.com/newborn-care/) or well-child [appointment](https://www.portlandpediatric.com/well-child-care/), ask your pediatrician or the pediatric P.A. or N.P. which apps they recommend or find the most useful.

In the meantime, here are five of our favorite parenting apps. We’ve included one health-oriented app; the rest support full-spectrum aspects of parenting – from infancy to young adulthood.

### **1\. Child Health Tracker**

Created by the American Academy of Pediatrics, the [Child Health Tracker app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/child-health-tracker-from-healthychildren-org/id664576969) maintains your child’s pertinent medical information, health provider contacts, insurance info, and more in one easy-access location. It also includes current information on vaccines and boosters. We feel this is one of the only health apps (outside of your [pediatrician’s patient portal](https://panw.pcc.com/portal/session/new)) you need.

Diagnostic-oriented apps are no comparison to a one-on-one phone call with one of our nurses, available by calling our office any time of the day or night. After our normal weekday and weekend office hours, PANW’s phone lines become a 24/7 nurse hotline where you receive personalized recommendations or advice about what to do next.

### **2\. Baby Feeding Log**

Are you a new parent? If so, you know that keeping track of feedings is far easier said than done when you’re completely sleep deprived or if other caregivers are in the mix to help out. The [Baby Feeding Log](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/baby-feeding-log/id412360317) is a simple way to tap when you’re feeding or just fed Baby.

If [you’re breastfeeding](https://www.portlandpediatric.com/lactation-feeding-support/), it helps to keep track of which breast they fed from to keep yourself comfortable and the Baby sufficiently fed. The app also helps parents and caregivers track the length of feedings, diaper changes, and sleep patterns. This information is helpful for you, but it also supplies excellent data to your pediatrician if any red flags arise and we want to know more about eating, hydration, and bowel habits.

### **3\. Our Family Wizard**

Are you part of a co-parenting family? If so, you’re going to love [Our Family Wizard](https://www.ourfamilywizard.com/). It’s one of the original co-parenting apps but continues to be one of the most popular. Repeat studies prove children thrive and do best when separated or divorced parents rise above their issues and maintain an amicable co-parenting dynamic.

Children of parents who remain respectful and keep their business out of the children’s lives have less anxiety, [perform better in school](https://www.portlandpediatric.com/back-to-school-tips/) and in friendships, and have fewer mental health issues. Healthy communication is essential to that mission, and Our Family Wizard supports that goal by keeping all of the schedules in an open and transparent location. In addition to shared calendar information, the app also tracks messages, banking info, and more.

### **4\. Artkive**

What the heck is a parent to do with all of the art and miscellaneous projects that come down the pike week after week, season after season, and year after year? Why, we [Artkive](https://www.artkiveapp.com/) them, of course. There’s no way we can keep all the stuff kids bring home, and more than one kid means exponentially more to store. Fortunately, Artkive makes it easy to take pictures and store memories of projects that don’t make the Top 5 list at the end of each year.

Artkive allows parents and guardians to have one reasonably sized storage tote per child for the absolute best of the mementos. The rest are organized on Artkive. You can create individual folders for each child that stores photos of their work by date. If you want, you can even print Artkive books, posters, framed works, canvases, and other space-saving options to gift to family or store for your children when they’re all grown up.

### **5\. Life360**

Remember when you thought tracking apps were a bit invasive? Then your Baby grew into an adolescent and teenager – and then they started to drive. Yep! Time to install [Life360](https://www.life360.com/). When you’re not spending time together as a family, Life360 helps you keep track of where everyone’s at.

In addition to location sharing, Life360 also includes a driving safety feature for parents of new drivers. The app tracks top speeds and driving habits and also provides crash detection, emergency dispatch, and roadside assistance. You’ll [sleep better](https://www.portlandpediatric.com/health-sleep-habits-for-the-whole-family/) when your independent kiddos have the freedom they crave paired with healthy parenting boundaries.

### **Bonus Parenting Apps**

These are some of the most essential apps for growing families. However, it’s not easy to put all of our favorites into a Top Five list. Others worth checking out depending on your family’s needs are:

**[• Modern Mama’s Club.](https://www.modernmamasclub.com/)** Download this app, and you may recognize someone – our very own Dr. Whitney Casares! Through this app, she shares guided lessons through her signature teachings, and you’ll uncover interactive journeys each day—integrating tools and tips into your daily life, diminishing burnout, stress, and anxieties—all while raising resilient children.

**[• Talk Space.](https://www.talkspace.com/)** A simple way to speak with licensed mental health professionals about [personal struggles](https://www.portlandpediatric.com/5-signs-of-postpartum-blues/), self-doubts, or any red flags you notice in your children’s mental/emotional well-being.

**[• Photomath](https://photomath.com/en)**. Nothing is more humbling than the inability to help a child with their homework. If you don’t use it, you lose it. Photomath allows parents to take pictures of the problem and receive steps on how to help kids solve it.

[**• Cozi Family Organizer**](https://www.cozi.com/). The name of the app says it all. The entire family has access to color-coded schedules, store lists, and other planning tools to keep in sync.

[**• Yummly**](https://www.yummly.com/). Not sure what to make for dinner with what you’ve got? Yummly does. The app also supports menu planning for picky eaters and recipes that break you out of the weekly dinner ruts.

### **PANW Is Here For The Questions Parenting Apps Don’t Answer**

Have a question that requires a deeper answer than a parenting app provides? Contact [Pediatric Associates of the Northwest](https://www.portlandpediatric.com/) online or by calling our office at 503-227-0671. Our lines provide 24/7 nurse advice over the phone after normal business hours.

![best baby apps](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/best-baby-apps-1625586970.png?crop=0.470xw:0.939xh;0.282xw,0.0288xh&resize=640:*)

apple//Getty Images

We've been independently researching and testing products for over 120 years. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission. Learn more about our [review process.](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/institute/about-the-institute/a19748212/good-housekeeping-institute-product-reviews/)

All of the parenting clichés are true, especially the one about your baby's first year being the longest and shortest time of your life. Each day is oh so long, but then the first birthday comes and you're like, "What happened to my newborn?"

At least now there are **baby tracker apps that help new parents** through the crazy first 12 months. For this list, [Good Housekeeping Institute](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/about/institute/) experts shared their favorite apps and we interviewed additional parents and testers to be sure we're recommending genuinely valuable downloads. Best news: While many apps offer premium features for extra money, a majority of testers found that free versions work well.

![huckleberry app logo for baby tracking](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/screenshot-2025-02-18-at-2-36-08-pm-67b4e1324a9ca.png?crop=0.716xw:0.722xh;0.129xw,0.115xh)Huckleberry Labs Inc.

1

## Best Newborn and Infant Tracker: Huckleberry

[Huckleberry](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fhuckleberrycare.com%2F) helps you track all babycare — but especially sleep — then evaluates trends and presents summaries. "I used Huckleberry for both kids for the first few months," says [Stefani Sassos](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/author/224673/stefani-sassos/), M.S., R.D., director of the [Good Housekeeping Institute](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/about/institute/a19748212/good-housekeeping-institute-product-reviews/) Nutrition Lab and a mom of a baby and preschooler. "It was helpful in the newborn days to keep track of feedings, nursing sessions, medications, and even poops and pee. It’s user-friendly and you can easily share the data with your pediatrician."

Another user praised how both parents can track, saying, "More than one person can use the app to update the baby's schedule, and it's an all-in-one place to log sleep, feeding, solids, diapers, pumping and even activities like baths, story time and tummy time."

If you have twins, you can track multiple kids. A tester said, "I loved the timed notifications. We needed to wake our daughters for feeds and it was stressful while sleep deprived. But as long as we logged feeds, Huckleberry calculated the wake-ups for us and set automatic alarms which was amazing!" _Free; premium versions for $5/month to $10/month include the brand's [SweetSpot](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fhuckleberrycare.com%2Fblog%2Fhow-to-use-our-magical-sleep-predictor-sweetspot) suggestions for naps and nighttime, and the more expensive one presents a week-by-week sleep plan_

[iOS](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fapps.apple.com%2Fus%2Fapp%2Fhuckleberry-baby-child%2Fid1169136078) [ANDROID](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.huckleberry_labs.app)

![the wonder weeks](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/best-baby-apps-wonder-weeks-1625164757.png?crop=0.825xw:0.825xh;0.0714xw,0.0935xh)The Wonder Weeks

2

## Best Behavior Tracker: The Wonder Weeks

Many parents told us that [The Wonder Weeks](https://www.thewonderweeks.com/) helped them figure out their **baby's moods** during the crucial infant months when it's hard to know what a newborn is so upset about. It's a long slog through the first month or two until you get that first smile!

Researchers behind the app identified mental leaps that every baby makes. Infants are more prone to crying, clinging and being cranky during those changes. This app helps you identify the waves and ride them. "There are Wonder Weeks Facebook groups for each month, too, if that's your thing," a user told us.

"The Wonder Weeks gave us an idea of what to expect in an easy format," a tester told us. "I think some people are literal about it and expect X to happen on Y day, but I just took the explanations as a guideline. It helped us get an idea of what might be going on and helped us feel like we weren't alone in the trenches." _Free for one week, $5/month, $10/three months, $35/two years_

[iOS](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fapps.apple.com%2Fapp%2Fthe-wonder-weeks%2Fid529815782) [ANDROID](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.twisevictory.apps.ex&pcampaignid=web_share)

Advertisement - Continue Reading Below

![black and white logo for the bump pregnancy baby tracker](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/screenshot-2025-02-18-at-3-23-15-pm-67b4ec8290b3d.png?crop=0.842xw:0.862xh;0.0612xw,0.0662xh)The Knot Inc

3

## Best Free Pregnancy Tracker: The Bump

Information relevant to your pregnancy **arrives every day** on [The Bump](https://www.thebump.com/)'s app. Users love to laugh at popular features like "how big is baby" food size comparisons, but it's a genuinely great tool for everything from [baby name](https://www.thebump.com/baby-names) inspiration to reading health advice.

While The Bump rose to the top of the the list for free pregnancy trackers, our testers also gave high marks to the [What to Expect](https://www.whattoexpect.com/mobile-app/) and [BabyCenter](https://www.babycenter.com/mobile-apps) apps, if you're looking for close runners-up. All offer communities you can join, for instance being in with a group of people due the same month. Experiences differ; some users say a community is a lifeline and some say comments give them anxiety, with a lot of in-between, but it's all free to try. _Free_

[iOS](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fapps.apple.com%2Fus%2Fapp%2Fpregnancy-baby-app-the-bump%2Fid568940747) [ANDROID](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.xogrp.thebump)

**RELATED:** [The Best Pregnancy Apps for Expecting](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/health/g36095216/best-pregnancy-tracker-apps/) [Parents](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/health/g36095216/best-pregnancy-tracker-apps/)

![silhouette of a fetus which is the logo for the pregnancy plus pregnancy tracking app](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/screenshot-2025-02-18-at-3-41-57-pm-67b4f0a28cb85.png?crop=0.656xw:0.719xh;0.179xw,0.140xh)Philips Digital UK Limited

4

## Best For-Fee Pregnancy Tracker: Pregnancy+

A winner of one of our most recent Parenting Awards, [Pregnancy+](https://philips-digital.com/pregnancy-new/) is a little more medical in feel, full of information and **detailed, interactive 3D models** of what's going on inside. If you like videos, our testers found the ones in this app to be helpful.

“I liked that it gave me a timeline so I was able to see what my body and baby were going through and things I should be looking out for,” said Senior Reviews Writer & Analyst [Olivia Lipski](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/author/231562/olivia-lipski/), a mom of an infant. She also liked the health and nutrition articles targeted to a user’s pregnancy stage. _Free; premium version_ _to access the 3D models for $4/month or $30/year_

[iOS](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fapps.apple.com%2Fus%2Fapp%2Fpregnancy-tracker-app%2Fid505864483) [ANDROID](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.hp.pregnancy.lite&_branch_match_id=1343363535302540565)

5

## Best Milestone Tracker: Pathways.org Baby Milestones

This also won our [Parenting Award](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/childrens-products/a61600413/good-housekeeping-parenting-awards-2024/), where we praised it for being a **free way to track key milestones**, new abilities and more. "Since it's free, it's worth downloading and checking it out," a tester told us. "The same content might also be on the [Pathways.org](https://pathways.org/milestones) site but the app is searchable and has a nice checklist."

“It’s a fantastic resource for activities to do with your baby and incredibly helpful any time you’re just sitting there wondering, _OK, well what should we do_?” another tester said. [Pathway’s YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@PathwaysBaby) is also integrated into the app. _Free_

[iOS](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fapps.apple.com%2Fus%2Fapp%2Fpathways-org-baby-milestones%2Fid1630421307) [ANDROID](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.pathwaysapp)

## Best Newborn Log: Glow Baby

In the first weeks, you want to capture all the data: feedings, diaper changes, sleep and more. The [Glow](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fglowing.com%2Fapps%23glow) family of apps includes a period tracker and pregnancy tracker, but we like the Baby app for **quickly logging babycare details,** and for the helpful interactive growth charts.

You can also connect to the rest of the Glow community to ask all those "is this normal?" questions. You have to pay a premium to unlock extra features like the ability to sync data across multiple caregivers. Testers also gave high marks to [Sprout Baby](https://sprout-apps.com/), [Baby Connect](https://www.babyconnect.com/) and [Baby Tracker](https://nighp.com/babytracker/), though Glow Baby was the favorite. _Free_ _; premium versions for_ _$16 to $60_

7

## Best for Developmental Activities: BabySparks

Okay, so what do you _do_ with your baby all day? [BabySparks](https://babysparks.com/app-overview/) offers tips for **parent-child playtime activities** tailored to your baby's age and stage, for babies from birth to age 3.

You'll get information on what's going on in baby's brain during these activities, and how the playtime is working gross-motor skills, fine-motor skills or other areas, like memory. You can also keep track of developmental milestones in this app. _Free for two activities a day_ _; premium versions for_ _$4 to $24 for more activities or parenting classes_

[iOS](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fapps.apple.com%2Fus%2Fapp%2Fbabysparks-development-app%2Fid794574199) [ANDROID](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.babysparks.babysparks)

![tinybeans](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/best-baby-apps-tinybeans-1625171280.jpeg?crop=1xw:1xh;center,top)Tinybeans

8

## Best for Sharing Photos: Tinybeans

"I really love [Tinybeans](https://tinybeans.com/) as a way to **share photos with family** that's not public," a user told us. Since many parents have privacy concerns around posting photos of their babies on social media, this offers a secure place to store and share photos with only the friends and family you invite, who also download the app.

You can add cute things like stickers and filters and you can print photo books for all the proud relatives. _Free_ _; premium version for unlimited storage and an ad-free experience_ _from $8 to $75_

[iOS](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fapps.apple.com%2Fus%2Fapp%2Ftinybeans-family-photo-album%2Fid521633042) [ANDROID](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tinybeans&hl=en_US&gl=US)

9

## Best On-Demand Medical Advice: Blueberry Pediatrics

You're going to have health questions about your baby, and issues aren't always going to present themselves when your doctor's in the office. While you still need an in-person pediatrician, [Blueberry Pediatrics](https://blueberrypediatrics.com/) offers **live, 24/7 virtual access to doctors**, and they'll give you a medical kit so you can take vitals at home.

Their experts can make diagnoses, send in prescriptions and recommend next steps while you and your baby are still in pajamas. With the pandemic rise of virtual visits through many doctors and insurance companies, Blueberry is no longer unique, but it's still a great service for anyone who doesn't have access through those other channels. _Free apps; membership to use the service is $18/month or $216/year_

[iOS](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fapps.apple.com%2Fus%2Fapp%2Fblueberry-pediatrics%2Fid1444477436) [ANDROID](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.blueberrypediatrics.blueberrypediatrics)

![sittercity and urbansitter](https://hips.hearstapps.com/hmg-prod/images/best-baby-apps-sittercity-urbansitter-1625165287.png?crop=1xw:1xh;center,top)Sittercity/UrbanSitter

10

## Best Baby Apps for Finding Care: Sittercity and UrbanSitter

Both [Sittercity](https://www.sittercity.com/) and [Urbansitter](https://www.urbansitter.com/) let you either browse profiles of **babysitters and nannies** for hire, or post a job listing and let caregivers respond to it (which is great if you're in a last-minute bind). The services do background checks, and you can read reviews from other parents before you book. Sittercity is iOS-only for its app. _Free apps; both require a membership fee to use their services, $9 to $200 depending on your location and membership duration_

## Best for Making Mom Friends: Peanut

Finding other parents who are on the same page as you can be difficult, so [Peanut](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.peanut-app.io%2F) seeks to make the whole process less socially awkward. You can **meet and chat with other local moms** through the app, join subject groups to cast a wider net or just read comments to see what everyone else is going through — no pressure! It's a way to check in with others without having to gather up the courage to start conversations with strangers on the playground. _Free; premium versions for $9 to $15_

[iOS](https://go.redirectingat.com/?id=74968X1525078&url=https%3A%2F%2Fapps.apple.com%2Fus%2Fapp%2Fpeanut-find-friends-support%2Fid1178656034) [ANDROID](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.teampeanut.peanut&hl=en_US&gl=US)

## Best for Finding Classes: KidPass

The [KidPass](https://kidpass.com/) app is iPhone-only. On it, you can discover **local baby classes**, mommy and me yoga and more, including classes for older kids ready for soccer, acting and the like. It's a boon to parents looking to get out and meet other families with kids the same age. The larger the city you live in, the more possibilities this app will serve up; on the [Instagram page](https://www.instagram.com/kidpass/?hl=en) the brand makes it clear this is currently best for parents in New York City, Los Angeles, Washington, D.C. and San Francisco.

The app is free, but if you buy a KidPass membership, you'll get a certain amount of credits each month that you can put toward the cost of a class. _Free; membership starts at $49/month_

Access hundreds of thousands of **baby songs, lullabies and playlists — not to mention parenting podcasts** — on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/) with one hand while you soothe your baby with the other.

You can also make your own playlists of baby favorites, and find your own music and playlists, too, for when you have some adult time. _Free; premium versions for an ad-free experience or family sharing for $12 to $20/month_

Streeterville Pediatrics


Apps for Parents, Families, and Kids

In this section, we hope to recommend various Apps that you may use to guide you through parenthood.  We will continue to update this list, and hope to get some valuable input and suggestions from our parents.  Please feel free to recommend and share apps that have been helpful for you - these may be seen in the “Suggested Apps From Other Parents” Section.

FIRST OF ALL:

One of the most important things you can do isMAKE AN ONGOING DOCUMENT OF YOUR CHILD’S HEALTH SUMMARY.  You can make a **Google Doc** or Apple Pages Document that you can continually update and add to. This way you can always access this information if you are ever out of town, at the emergency room, or if school/camp needs to know your child’s immunization status.  And, all of this can be available to you on your mobile device no matter where you are!  This will be an invaluable tool for you - believe me!

Click on these links to see a [SUGGESTED TEMPLATE](https://www.streetervillepediatrics.com/suggested-personal-medical-record-document.html)and an [EXAMPLE](https://www.streetervillepediatrics.com/example-of-a-personal-medical-record-document.html)of this ongoing document.

Suggested Apps for New Parents

By Dr McCabe

Baby Connect ($4.99) - good app for feeding tracking

Allows parents to easily track information such as feedings, diapers, naps, milestones, mood, pumpings, medicines, vaccines and growth. Breastfeeding mothers can use a timer to easily record the time and breast for each feeding.  Parents can compare with the previous day and previous week averages, and view the data on graphs to identify trends.  Data automatically syncs on multiple devices.  Alarms can be set to notify when it’s time for the next feeding or diaper change or medicine dose, etc.  Parents can also enter free form notes.

iBaby Feed Timer ($4.99) - good app for feeding tracking

Designed for breastfeeding mothers to track breastfeeds (a timer and pause button to record which side and for how long), bottle feeds, breast pumps, diapers, sleep, solid food, weight, and length.  Parents can also set reminders and enter notes.  Analyzes data and shows daily, weekly, and monthly averages.  Data can be plotted on graphs to easily see trends, and data can sync on multiple devices.

Baby Bundle (free) - good free app for all around baby tracking

Baby Bundle also tracks things like feedings, diapers, sleep, vaccines and growth.  Besides tracking, it gives a guide on what to expect at your next pediatrician’s appointment, acts as a rudimentary baby book, and provides a health reference and baby care guide.  Parents can check off the milestones and the day it happened - and add it (theoretically) to a bound baby book later.  It was developed in partnership with a pediatrician and mom, so the health reference and baby care guides can be trusted.

Baby Sprout - ($4.99) good pay app for all around baby tracking

Baby Sprout also has all of the tracking tools and planners, but is especially good for milestones and development.  Parents can record milestones, memories, photos, and captions. Monthly updates on developmental milestones enable parents to see how their child is faring.  A plentiful supply of food tracking allows parents to easily see how solids are going.  A medical record tool allows parents to keep track of sick and healthy check-ups.

WebMD Baby (free) - good app for medical advice

WebMD Baby offers medical advice tailored to a baby’s specific age.  It has hundreds of articles, tips, and videos on baby and toddler care, illnesses and emergencies, tips for mom, tips for dad, parenting tips, milestones, vaccines, and doctor visits.  It offers weekly content packages suited to a baby’s current age.  It also allows parents to track sleep, diapers growth, feedings, and milestones.

Baby Shusher (free)

This app creates the rhythmic shushing noise that helps crying babies relax and potentially fall asleep.  It comes with a timer and a sound equalizer, which allows the volume to increase if a baby starts to cry.

Suggested Apps for All Parents

Car Seat Check ($1.99)

This app allows parents to quickly learn what car seat is right for their child based on age, weight, and height.  Installation videos, audio clips, and articles helps ensure that the car seat is used correctly.

Suggested Apps for Media Use

Common Sense Media / Kids Media (free)

This is a great app and website [www.Commonsensemedia.org](http://www.commonsensemedia.org/) that reviews movies, TV shows, books, games, etc for kids.  The recommendations are based on media type and age!  Go to the website for greater info and to get more info - you’ll get lost looking through this website.  Disclaimer - I’m not exactly sure who and how they really rate things, however, it looks like they have a reputable board that makes these suggestions.

AND - THE BEST APP OF ALL!!!!!

Streeterville Pediatrics (free)

This is our Pediatric Office website! Our website is full of helpful information: dosage charts, info to stay healthy, info on illnesses, practice information, etc.

Type in: [www.streetervillpediatrics.com](http://www.streetervillpediatrics.weebly.com/) and you can get the website and you can “Add to Home Screen” to have easy access to the website - mobile version. Clicking on the upper left corner will give you the index to the website. Enjoy!

Bringing a new life into this world is a magical experience - there's no question about that. But it also brings with it a whirlwind of changes, particularly for first-time parents.

The days of poring over manual records and relying solely on maternal instincts are long behind us, with technology now offering a helping hand through every stage of the child-rearing process, right from pregnancy to parenting the toddler years.

In this post, we'll walk you through the best apps for new parents - designed to streamline your daily tasks, ease your anxieties, and create the reassuring sense of community that every parent needs.

## Why You Should Download a Few New Apps

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/5f9e3058e3ecc6040724fa97/66184f11b5c3259561969ce3_0-XAHu9EqokYlKWqdY9EbyWxiXb0SQr2DiZ2YbHgSCOqHavvAWRFIkdR9raiYDEJBqz6Hd105hw9I2Nqysztg8GWBvcSrwrIHNbU5HZa7zjJHerZWQBAVgiXUJ_rLpe3ekFUJ3XoFG4PHybQJ4ZMex4.png)

When it comes to parenting, the phrase "it takes a village" isn't just a saying - it's a modus operandi. Whether it's for tracking feeding times, decoding developmental milestones, or just finding a like minded community, new parents can benefit significantly from the right set of apps.

With smartphone use increasing substantially over the years, it only makes sense to digitize parenting in a way that's not just convenient but also intuitive and supportive.

### Get Immediate Assistance and Answers to Your Questions

In those frantic moments of your baby crying inconsolably or a mysterious rash appearing, an app with a direct line to expert advice is a godsend.

These platforms not only provide the answers you need at a swipe but can also connect you with pediatricians and specialists for in-depth consultations.

### Help You Track Feedings and Sleep

The days blend into one another with sleep-deprived hazes, but keeping a digital log of feedings and sleep patterns can help you spot trends and make sure your little one is healthy and on track.

### Keep an Eye on Developmental Milestones

In the blur of early parenthood, it’s easy to lose track of your baby’s development. An app that details what to expect and when can both reassure and inform parents about their child’s growth.

### Record Memories

From the first smile to the first steps, [every milestone deserves to be remembered](https://www.getearlybird.io/blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-finding-the-right-app-to-record-family-stories) and cherished. Apps like [EarlyBird](https://www.getearlybird.io/) that help you keep track of these moments are invaluable in creating a lasting record of your child's formative years.

### Access Educational Materials

With volumes of information out there, finding the best pearls of parenting wisdom can be a chore without a guiding hand.

Many apps curate and provide essential reading material that's just a download away. You can learn about anything and everything, from why your toddler is doing that weird nose picking thing to how to have those difficult conversations with your mother in law.

### Build a Sense of Community

Talking to others who have experienced - or are currently experiencing - what you're going through can offer a level of empathy and understanding that's hard to find anywhere else. Many apps have built-in features that allow you to connect with other parents around the world (or even right in your hometown).

### Improve Communication

Sometimes, it’s tricky to keep all caregivers on the same page. Apps that sync data and communication can ensure that every caretaker, from mom to dad to grandma and even the daycare teacher, has the exact information they need about the baby’s schedule and needs.

### Boost Organization and Time Management

From tracking vaccinations to planning the day's activities, an app can make sure that you're in control, always with a handle on what needs to be done.

## Tips for Choosing the Best App as a New Parent

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/5f9e3058e3ecc6040724fa97/66184f1125967eeb19675083_-Scj2nRZAr7mSWsB4EFBlz72V0sb6vsbwJdu8joM_sLQQXuO6zfYP6gWMygTzjIzjC5X23H14GeWEH2IT52tBa8IE4t73D89ggDQnXu5I047IPBGNmTREPALvLrXVGflFxfxtgcrBOLWZG5XwIHuqLA.png)

Before you start downloading every app that promises to make baby care easier, consider these tips to find the best fit for you and your family's needs.

### Consider the Learning Curve

You're likely to be wrestling with sleep deprivation, so look for apps with an intuitive design that doesn't require a NASA scientist to decode.

### Read the Reviews

Real-world parents can provide insight into the app’s benefits and drawbacks. Pay attention to what they say to avoid any unpleasant surprises post-installation.

### Look for Customization

Babies are as varied as the parents who raise them. An app that caters to your individual schedule and baby's needs will be far more useful than a generic one-size-fits-all platform.

### Check for Live Support

Immediate access to medical professionals can provide peace of mind when you're dealing with common concerns or need a second opinion.

### Opt for Synchronization with Multiple Devices

If you'll share caregiving duties, a seamless experience across all devices can keep everyone in the loop without the need for constant updates.

### Think About Longevity

The best apps are those that will grow with you and your child, offering support not just in the newborn days but also for toddlers and beyond.

## Best Apps for New Parents

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/5f9e3058e3ecc6040724fa97/66184f11606d4ab1ba2dbf7c_wgGsBsZ1MZu-Cj_2h3B1o0lnLLp-zDTbqGocIi6-DYHzj4sWDCqKy7VuPgxU02ecYt6OjVF2pfsniet0X-mKqjJXxHaGny1HDeYY4aFYx_Z-_Qv1U7rxZi2phCxeQDoR2NclzNjqfYM9gHTBRv8d9Kc.png)

Now that you know what to look for (and why) here are some of the best apps you can choose from to support and guide you through the first precious years of early parenthood.

### 1\. EarlyBird

For new parents who want to create a digital time capsule for their child, EarlyBird is the app of choice.

It’s a secure and private space where you can [store memories](https://www.getearlybird.io/blog/why-saving-memories-is-important-for-your-childs-development), along with the ability for family and friends to add to it.

EarlyBird also includes a financial growth option, allowing family and friends to make digital investment in your child’s future. The app provides a seamless combination of sentimental and practical features to help you treasure these moments and secure the future.

### 2\. Summer Health

[Summer Health](https://summerhealth.com/) extends healthcare beyond the doctor’s office with its Everyday Care concierge service.

Offering personalized access to pediatricians and specialists 24/7, the app is designed to handle urgent issues and provide ongoing guidance.

In addition, it provides 1-on-1 support for areas like sleep, nutrition, and lactation, offering a holistic approach to child healthcare.

### 3\. Maple

Staying organized as a parent can be a gargantuan task, but with [Maple](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/maple-household-planner/id1551070188), organization becomes intuitive. It serves as a comprehensive household management app, from meal planning and shopping lists to family calendaring.

Maple’s AI-powered “Fast” feature takes much of the planning off your plate, making sure that you’re never caught off guard with your parenting and household duties - as a result, guaranteeing that your focus can be entirely on nurturing your growing family.

### 4\. Huckleberry

[Huckleberry](https://huckleberrycare.com/) is a true one-stop baby & parenting app. Designed to track and optimize your child's sleep, feeding, growth, nutrition, and much more, Huckleberry is a versatile companion for the exhaustive demands of parenthood.

Its SweetSpot feature intuitively predicts your child's next nap time, simplifying the complexities of the sleep schedule. It goes beyond the traditional baby tracker and offers expert guidance that grows with your child.

### 5\. Hatch

[Hatch](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hatch-sleep/id1158048301) offers a suite of products and a companion app to facilitate better sleep for your child (and yourself!).

With features to create the perfect sleep environment and guide your baby through healthy sleep patterns, Hatch is poised to be a welcome addition to any new parent’s toolkit. The Rest, Rest+, and Restore features adapt to your child’s specific sleep needs at different stages, offering both flexibility and support.

### 6\. SolidStarts

When it’s time to introduce solid foods to your child, you want to be informed and confident. [SolidStarts](https://solidstarts.com/) provides extensive information on the when, how, and what of feeding your child, including nutrition details, tips on preparation, and videos of real babies eating the foods.

Its paid subscription offers a robust tracking feature to personalize the experience of food introduction and identify any food-related issues early on.

### 7\. Dyper

While not a traditional parenting app, [Dyper](https://dyper.com/) provides efficient diapering and supply solutions for busy parents. It's all about making the essentials - diapers - simpler and more sustainable.

With an intuitive browsing interface and user-friendly checkout, the app ensures that you’re always stocked up on the necessities. It also offers exclusive access to collection launches and discounts, focusing on the convenience side of parenting apps.

### 8\. Nanit

[Nanit](https://www.nanit.com/) is the tool for parents who need more visibility into their baby’s sleep patterns.

Using computer vision, Nanit offers insights into how your baby is sleeping, including if they’re fussy, awake, or sleeping soundly.

## The Takeaway

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/5f9e3058e3ecc6040724fa97/66184f11e5739ceb6c9bfb80_6okXIWpBHt5NEMhKKOgvul8KpZVjZ4NOMvF0Vz79DixQ1pYxQDXbgdVQcGbrf6MVHp0F9e6nBh2flIq1zWwI8RcskmID2UABygj-LRnovgNwXiZ3obfBDV58MFEUh4B7jFMbDW8HZnDT-ETRqPOlf5Y.png)

Instead, look at these digital tools as allies that can help you find more time and energy to be present with your little one. If you're feeling overwhelmed, take a deep breath, and know that you're doing great.

And if you're still searching for that perfect app, consider downloading the EarlyBird app to start your parenting adventure on the right foot. ## Quick Answer

**The best parenting apps do one useful job really well, like tracking feeds, sleep, growth, or reminders. Parents need a “best by use case” guide, not just a long general list.**

[Book Appointment](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/book-appointment/) [New Parent Visits](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/services/wellness-visits/)

### When to call

- An app is making you more anxious instead of more organized.
- You are relying on app advice instead of getting help for feeding, fever, breathing, or growth concerns.
- You want a real pediatric follow-up for newborn or parenting questions.

### Quick FAQs

What should new parents actually track?

Usually feeds, wet diapers, sleep patterns, growth concerns, and reminders for visits or vaccines matter most.

Can parenting apps replace a pediatrician?

No. They can help organize information, but they should not replace medical evaluation when a child is sick or not doing well.

### Helpful next steps

['](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/() ['](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/()

## Table of Contents

Parenthood is a great, exciting, and joyful journey for new moms, but it comes with tons of tasks. New moms strive to be super moms!  They keep track of feedings, doctor visits, sleep patterns, diaper changes, and many more.

Many [parenting apps](https://tinybeans.com/best-apps-for-moms/) are available today to help new moms manage their parenting responsibilities and simplify their lives. But first, let’s talk about some of the top parenting apps for new moms. The best picks will suit your needs and preferences.

### 1.   WebMD Baby

![toddlers](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

WebMD Baby is a reliable parenting app that provides customized advice to new mothers. The app offers information on parenting topics, including breastfeeding, baby development, nutrition, safety, sleep, and comfort and soothing techniques.

The WebMD Baby app also comes with a symptom checker that helps new moms determine if their child is experiencing any health problems. Additionally, this app offers a journal where moms can record the daily activities and milestones of their babies.

### 2.   BabyCenter

BabyCenter is one of the awesome parenting apps that offers customized advice and support to new moms. It gives information on parenting topics such as baby development milestones, feeding and nutrition, safety, sleep, and health.

Also, the BabyCenter app comes with a moms’ forum where they can connect and share experiences. It also offers helpful tools such as a contraction timer, a baby growth chart, and a baby name finder.

### 3.   The Wonder Weeks

![Mother multi-tasking with infant daughter in home office telehealth for kids](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Wonder Weeks is a trusted app that helps new moms understand the development and behavior of their babies. The app provides a calendar that tracks the baby’s age. It offers information on the various developmental stages that the child is going through.

The Wonder Weeks parenting app offers information on the baby’s sleep patterns, moods, and behavior during each stage. Also, it helps new moms know their babies’ intrinsic needs and offers handy tips to soothe and calm their babies.

### 4.   Baby Tracker

Baby Tracker is a fantastic parenting app that helps new moms keep track of their baby’s diaper changes, feedings, growth, sleep patterns, and developmental milestones. Moms can closely monitor their babies’ daily activities using its easy-to-use interface.

The Baby Tracker app also lets new moms track their breastfeeding sessions, such as the side they feed on as well as the duration of the feeding. In addition, this parenting app provides many helpful tips and guidance for new mothers.

### 5.   Peanut

Peanut is an amazing social networking application that connects new mothers with other mothers in their area. This parenting app offers a platform where moms can connect, share experiences, and seek advice.

The parenting app also offers helpful features like calendaring since moms can schedule playdates, a chat feature, and a directory where they can find local resources as well as services.

### 6.   Cozi Family Organizer

The Cozi Family Organizer app helps new moms manage the activities and schedules of their families. The app comes with a shared calendar that lets mothers schedule activities, appointments, and events for their entire family.

This parenting app offers moms a to-do list where they can generate and allocate tasks to other family members. Also, the parenting app offers a shopping list feature, allowing moms to create and share their grocery lists.

### 7.   Baby Connect

Baby Connect is an amazing parenting application that helps new moms trace the daily activities of their babies. Moms can track their babies’ feedings, nap behavior, medication, and even diaper changes.

Baby Connect offers a great dashboard that shows all the activities and lets mothers watch the progress of their babies. It comes with a sharing feature that allows moms to share their baby’s activities with other family members.

A timeline feature is also added to show a summary of the child’s activities.

### 8.   Tinybeans

Tinybeans is a great parenting app that helps new moms generate and showcase a baby journal with their loved ones. It offers a secure platform where mothers can upload images and videos of their babies’ milestones and share them with family or friends.

Tinybeans also has a calendar feature, allowing moms to track their babies’ playdates, development, and appointments. Also, the parenting app allows moms to generate a custom timeline of the growth and progress of their babies.

### 9.   White Noise Baby

White Noise Baby is another amazing parenting app with calming sounds and lullabies to help new moms calm and soothe their babies. The app offers a variety of sounds, such as rain, lullabies, ocean waves, and white noise.

These great sounds can help babies sleep better. Additionally, the parenting app offers a timer feature, allowing moms to set a particular duration for the sound to play.

You might be interested in a related topic on white noise; [this article](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/the-science-behind-white-noise-your-baby/) is for you: White Noise: The Science Behind Soothing Sounds for Your Baby’s Peaceful Sleep.

### 10.  BabySparks

BabySparks is a significant parenting app that offers developmentally suitable activities for babies. This parenting app for new moms offers a customized plan for babies based on their age, developmental stage, and milestones.

[📅 Book an Appointment](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/book-appointment/)

Same-day and next-day appointments available.

BabySparks comes with a variety of activities, such as playtime, motor skill development, and sensory activities. Also, the parenting app offers video tutorials for moms to make sure they are successfully engaging in the activities.

## Parenting Apps for New Moms: Their Advantages

![parenting-apps](<Base64-Image-Removed>)

Parenting applications have become a famous tool for moms because of the many advantages they provide. Check out this list of its remarkable advantages:

- Efficient monitoring and management of the baby’s daily routine, such as feeding, sleep, and diaper changes,
- Easy scheduling and supervision of pediatrician’s schedules and playdates.
- Connection with other parents through online forums or conversation groups for advice and recommendations.
- Access to educational resources similar to articles, videos, and expert advice on colorful aspects of child development, nutrition, and discipline
- Time-saving and stress-reducing by giving a central position for all parenthood needs, getting rid of the need for multiple sources of information and resources.
- Advanced association and planning of tasks, schedules, and liabilities
- Increased mindfulness and monitoring of the child’s development.
- Flexibility to customize features based on individual parenting styles and needs.
- Potential cost savings by avoiding the need for multiple specialized apps or tools

## What to Look for in a Parenting App

New mothers frequently find themselves struggling with the overwhelming responsibilities of [taking care of a baby](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/the-ultimate-baby-proofing-checklist/). Luckily, parenting apps have made their transition much easier.

However, with a wide array of parenting apps to choose from, choosing the appropriate one proves difficult. Here, we give you guidelines on what to look out for when searching for apps.

### User-Friendly Interface

As a new mom, you’ve already dealt with tons of stress, so the last thing you want is an application that adds frustration. The parenting app should have a straightforward interface that lets you easily use its features.

If the app is overly complicated to set up or difficult to navigate, busy moms will readily get uninterested and simply won’t use it.

### Makes a Mom’s Life Easier

Look for an app that has, if not all, the features you need. The features that are commonly needed are a sleep tracker, diaper tracker, feeding tracker, shared calendar, expense tracker, messenger, family plan template, online storage, and many more.

These features help new moms track their babies’ routines, which could significantly affect managing daily tasks.

### Relevant Information for the Baby’s Age

The information presented should be accurate, up-to-date, scientific, and research-based. It should contain relevant topics such as [breastfeeding](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/breastfeeding-moms-hear/), [developmental milestones](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/developmental-milestones-parents-must-know/), and [vaccinations](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/importance-of-routine-vaccinations/).

Consider your child’s age, since parenting apps lean heavily on a specific age group.

### Compatibility and Security

Ensure the app is compatible with your device. It should have strong securiEnsure the app is compatible with your device. It should have strong security measures in place to protect your personal information and data. Before you hit the switch, be sure to enable the app’s enhanced security features to keep the video streams of your baby private, accessible only by you.

**Steps to Secure Your Baby Monitoring App:**

1. **Check Compatibility**: Make sure the app works seamlessly with your device.
2. **Activate Enhanced Security Features**: Enable the app’s built-in security options to safeguard your video streams.
3. **Restrict Access**: Configure settings so that only you can access the video streams.

These actions will ensure that your baby’s video streams are secure and private, giving you peace of mind.ty measures in place to protect your personal information and data.

To enhance security, follow these additional steps:

- **Password Protection:** Make sure your Wi-Fi network is password-protected, and always use the strongest password possible. Avoid obvious choices like “password,” your birthday, or “123456.”
- **Avoid Web Uploads:** Resist the temptation to upload the monitor feed to the Web for sharing with friends and family. This can expose the feed to unauthorized access.

### Provides a Support Network and Connections

As a new mom who could feel lonely, having a community of like-minded people could be greatly helpful. However, it should come with a platform to connect with other [new mothers](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/importance-of-self-care-for-new-mothers/), ask queries, and share experiences.

## The Future of Parenting Apps for New Moms: Trends and Predictions

[Parenting apps](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/what-are-the-parenting-guides-for-newborns/) have been helpful for new mothers across the globe. These apps offer valuable insights into baby care, sleep patterns, feeding schedules, and lots more.

Parenting apps are becoming even more advanced, paving the way for a new era of baby care. Below are some trends and predictions:

- There will be a surge in the use of parenting applications. The apps are expected to analyze deep data and offer personalized guides to new moms based on the behavioral patterns of their babies.
- Parenting apps will be utilized to predict [possible health problems](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/8-common-childhood-illnesses/) and potential health hazards, enabling mothers to initiate preventive measures.
- Gamification will become a component of parenting apps to allow moms to engage in fun activities while using them. Moms will earn rewards for finishing tasks related to baby care, like feeding, putting the baby to sleep, or changing diapers.
- With the emergence of wearable electronic devices, it isn’t surprising that parenting apps will be integrated with smartwatches.
- As [social networking](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/social-media-affects-parental-loneliness/) gains popularity, moms can readily connect to seek advice and share common experiences.

## Harness the Beauty of Parenting Apps to Make Life Easy

Being a new mom can be overwhelming and challenging, yet full of joy and fulfillment. You need to meet the daily grind of baby care. Nonetheless, _**with the help of parenting apps, managing mom’s tasks could become easier and less stressful.**_

We at [Omega Pediatric](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/) s have come up with a list of parenting apps designed to [meet the demands of new moms](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/mistakes-new-moms-make-when-breastfeeding/). The apps cater to different aspects of parenting, such as tracking the child’s feeding and daily routines, as well as managing family schedules.

[Omega Pediatrics](https://www.omegapediatrics.com/omega-pediatrics-promo/) treats you and your baby as one family. As a new mom, we care for you as much as we do for our young patients. With parenting apps, new moms like you will be more confident in navigating their parenting journey. We are with you.

## FAQ

### **What are some recommended parenting apps for new moms?**

Some top picks include WebMD Baby, BabyCenter, The Wonder Weeks, Baby Tracker, and Peanut. These apps offer various features like customized advice, tracking baby development, connecting with other moms, and more.

### **How can parenting apps help new moms manage their daily tasks?**

Parenting apps efficiently monitor and manage tasks such as feeding, sleep, diaper changes, and pediatrician appointments. They also provide educational resources, connection with other parents, and centralized organization of parenting needs.

### **What should I look for in a parenting app?**

Look for apps with a user-friendly interface, features that meet your needs (such as sleep tracking, feeding tracking, shared calendar), accurate and relevant information, compatibility and security, and a supportive community.

### **What are some predicted trends in parenting apps for the future?**

Predictions include a surge in app usage, personalized guides based on baby’s behavior, predictive health analysis, gamification features, integration with wearable devices, and enhanced social networking capabilities for moms.

### **How can parenting apps enhance the experience of being a new mom?**

Parenting apps make daily tasks easier to manage, provide valuable insights into baby care, offer support networks for new moms, and contribute to a more confident and informed parenting journey.

### What are the The Advantages of Using a Baby Monitoring App Over a Traditional Baby Monitor

**Stay Connected Anywhere, Anytime**

One of the primary benefits of using a baby monitoring app is the unparalleled flexibility it offers. Unlike traditional baby monitors that have a limited range, smartphone-based monitors allow you to check on your baby from anywhere in the world. Whether you’re in a different room or halfway across the globe, as long as you have an internet connection, peace of mind is just a tap away.

**Ease of Setup**

Setting up a baby monitoring app is generally very straightforward. Most apps are designed with user-friendliness in mind, ensuring even the most sleep-deprived new parents can get them up and running quickly. Unlike traditional baby monitors, which can involve complicated installation and be prone to hardware issues, a baby monitoring app typically requires just a few simple steps to get started.

**Cost-Effective Solution**

Using a baby monitoring app can be more budget-friendly than investing in a traditional monitor. Many apps are available for free or at a much lower cost compared to dedicated baby monitoring devices. Plus, you can repurpose an old smartphone or tablet as the camera, making it an even more economical option.

**Enhanced Features**

Modern baby monitoring apps come loaded with advanced features that often surpass those of traditional monitors. These may include motion detection, sound alerts, recording capabilities, and even integration with other smart home devices. Some apps also offer options for two-way audio, allowing you to speak to and soothe your baby remotely.

**Multi-Device Access**

Another advantage is the ability to access the baby monitor feed on multiple devices simultaneously. This means both parents can monitor the baby from their respective devices, or even grandparents and babysitters can have access if needed. Traditional monitors typically restrict access to a single dedicated device, limiting flexibility.

**Portability and Convenience**

Since baby monitoring apps utilize your smartphone, which you’re likely already carrying, there’s no need for additional bulky equipment. This portability adds a layer of convenience, making it easier to go about your day while keeping an eye on your little one.

**Secure and Up-to-Date**

Security is a crucial consideration for any baby monitoring system. Many baby monitoring apps offer encrypted connections to keep your video feed secure. Regular app updates ensure that any security vulnerabilities are quickly addressed, providing an added layer of protection that may not be present in outdated traditional monitors.

By choosing a baby monitoring app, you gain not just peace of mind but a plethora of features and conveniences that traditional monitors simply can’t match. The bridge between technology and parenting has never been more seamless.

### Are There Any Free Baby Monitoring Apps Available?

Absolutely! There are several free baby monitoring apps that can help you keep an eye on your little one. One noteworthy option is an app available for Android users, which offers both audio and video streaming. This allows you to hear and see your baby in real-time, providing peace of mind no matter where you are.

Moreover, some apps also enable two-way communication, so you can talk to your baby remotely. This feature can be especially comforting for both you and your child, allowing for a semblance of closeness even when you’re physically apart.

If you’re looking for a cost-effective way to monitor your baby, these free apps are definitely worth considering.

### What Features Should I Look for in a Baby Monitoring App?

Choosing the right baby monitoring app can be daunting with so many options available. Here are key features to consider ensuring you select the best app for your family’s needs.

Video and Audio Streaming

Ensure the app provides both video and audio streaming. This capability allows you to see and hear your baby in real-time, giving you peace of mind while tending to other tasks. Look for high-resolution video and clear audio quality.

Noise and Motion Alerts

Apps equipped with noise and motion detection alerts will notify you immediately if your baby is restless or needs attention. Instant alerts ensure you’re always aware of your baby’s status without constantly monitoring the screen.

Remote Control Features

Remote control features are crucial for convenience. These can include the ability to play lullabies, white noise, or control a night light from your device. These functionalities help soothe your baby without needing to enter the room.

Wide Device Compatibility

Choose an app compatible with various devices, including smartphones, tablets, smartwatches, and computers. Dual compatibility with iOS and Android platforms ensures that all caregivers can connect, regardless of their device preference.

Secure Communication

Security is paramount when it comes to monitoring your baby. Look for apps that offer industry-standard encryption to protect the communication between your devices and the monitor.

Internet Connectivity

Ensure the app works seamlessly over both Wi-Fi and cellular networks. This flexibility allows you to stay connected with your baby no matter where you are, whether at home or away.

Multi-device Support

If multiple caregivers are involved, choose an app that supports the connection of multiple devices simultaneously. This feature allows everyone to stay updated and respond to the baby’s needs efficiently.

Additional Peripherals

Some apps offer integration with additional peripherals like Apple TV, Mac, PC, or Chromecast. These integrations transform your entertainment devices into baby monitoring stations, adding another layer of convenience.

When selecting a baby monitoring app, prioritizing these features will help you make an informed decision, ensuring both you and your baby remain connected and secure.

## Best Apps for Mothers: Stay Organized, Connected and Supported

Whether you're a new mom or an expecting parent, finding the right app can make a world of difference. Here are some of the best apps designed to help moms in various aspects of their lives:

### Organization Apps

Managing a household, juggling appointments and keeping track of daily tasks can feel overwhelming. Organization apps help busy moms streamline their responsibilities by offering tools for scheduling, task management and collaboration. Whether you need a digital planner, a shared family calendar or a place to store important notes, these top organization apps can make life a little easier.

- [Todoist:](https://www.todoist.com/) A productivity app that helps busy moms organize tasks, set reminders and manage family schedules. It allows users to prioritize activities, collaborate with family members and track progress to stay on top of responsibilities.

- [Evernote](https://evernote.com/): A digital notebook for keeping track of to-do lists, grocery shopping and parenting notes. With voice memos, document scanning and synchronization across devices, it's a powerful tool for managing family life.

- [Cozi](https://www.cozi.com/): A family organizer with shared calendars, grocery lists and meal planning. It helps parents coordinate schedules, assign chores and keep track of appointments in one convenient place.


### Health and Wellness Apps

Taking care of yourself is just as important as caring for your family. Health and wellness apps make it easier for moms to stay active, reduce stress and maintain a balanced lifestyle. Whether you’re looking for quick workouts, guided meditation or nutrition tracking, these apps provide the support you need to focus on your well-being.

- [Workout for Women](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.workoutinc.seven_7minutesfitness_forwomen&hl=en-US&pli=1): Quick and effective workouts tailored for busy moms. It features short, guided exercise routines that require minimal equipment, making fitness more accessible.

- [Calm](https://www.calm.com/): A meditation app perfect for reducing stress and promoting mindfulness. It offers sleep stories, guided meditations and breathing exercises to help moms find moments of peace.

- [Headspace](https://www.headspace.com/headspace-meditation-app): Offers guided meditation and relaxation techniques to [support mental health](https://milk-drunk.com/struggling-vs-suffering-supporting-postpartum-mental-health/). Designed for beginners and experienced meditators alike, it helps reduce anxiety and improve focus.

- [MyFitnessPal:](https://www.myfitnesspal.com/) Tracks diet and exercise, helping moms maintain a healthy lifestyle. With a vast food database and personalized goal tracking, it simplifies nutrition planning.


## Social Connection Apps

Motherhood can feel isolating at times, but you don’t have to navigate it alone. Social connection apps help moms find support, share experiences and build friendships with like-minded parents. Whether you’re looking for virtual advice, group discussions or in-person meetups, these apps make it easier to connect with a community that understands you.

- [Peanut](https://www.peanut-app.io/): Connects moms to a supportive community of fellow parents. It facilitates friendships, group chats and discussions on motherhood-related topics.

- [MomCircle](https://momcircle.com/): Provides parenting advice and support groups. It offers expert insights, community-driven discussions and a space to share experiences with other moms.

- [Meetup](https://www.meetup.com/): Enables moms to find and join local parenting groups. Whether looking for playdates, mom meetups or parenting workshops, this app makes in-person connections easier.


## Parenting Guidance Apps

Keeping track of your baby’s development, sleep patterns and [feeding](https://www.hibobbie.com/blogs/bobbieu/tagged/series-formula-feeding) schedule can be overwhelming, but parenting guidance apps simplify the process. These tools help parents monitor milestones, understand behavioral changes and coordinate care with ease. Whether you're tracking daily routines or gaining insight into developmental leaps, these apps provide invaluable support.

- [Baby Connect](https://www.babyconnect.com/login): A comprehensive baby-tracking app covering feeding, sleeping and milestones. It allows multiple caregivers to update logs, making coordination effortless.

- [The Wonder Weeks](https://thewonderweeks.com/): Provides insights into a baby’s developmental leaps. It helps parents understand behavioral changes and growth phases, offering guidance on how to support their child.

- [Glow Baby](https://glowing.com/apps): Tracks a baby’s developmental milestones, feeding and sleep schedules. It offers personalized insights based on pediatric guidelines.


## Financial Planning Apps

Managing family finances can be tricky, but the right apps can make it easier. From budgeting to finding discounts on baby essentials, these tools help parents stay on top of their expenses. Here's a quick look at the best apps for different types of moms to fit your unique needs.

- [Credit Karma](https://www.creditkarma.com/): Take control of your family's finances. It offers credit monitoring, personalized savings insights, and smart budgeting tools to help moms track spending, manage bills, and improve their financial well-being—all in one place

- [Flipp](https://flipp.com/): Saves money by finding local discounts and coupons for baby essentials. It compiles weekly flyers, helping parents maximize their savings on groceries and baby products.


## Best Apps for Different Types of Mothers

Not all moms have the same needs. Here’s a breakdown of [the best apps](https://fullheartmommy.com/new-mom-apps/) tailored for different parenting experiences:

Pregnant Mothers

- [The Bump](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.xogrp.thebump&hl=en-US): Tracks pregnancy week by week with expert articles and tips. It offers 3D interactive images of fetal development and personalized updates.

- [Ovia Pregnancy Tracker](https://www.oviahealth.com/pregnancy-app/): Monitors baby development and provides health insights. It includes symptom tracking, nutrition advice and customizable features.

- [WebMD Pregnancy](https://www.webmd.com/webmdapp?from=AppAgg.com): Provides expert-backed health information, symptom tracking and doctor-approved tips throughout pregnancy. It includes a pregnancy journal, checklists and personalized updates to help expectant mothers stay informed and prepared

- [What to Expect:](https://www.whattoexpect.com/mobile-app/) Guides moms-to-be through every stage of pregnancy with personalized updates, expert advice and a supportive community. It includes daily tips, [community forums](https://community.whattoexpect.com/forums/formula-feeding.html), development tracking and interactive tools to help expectant mothers feel informed and prepared.


New Mothers

- [Baby Tracker](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.nighp.babytracker_android&hl=en-US): Helps track diaper changes, feeding and sleep schedules. It ensures new moms stay informed about their baby’s daily routines.

- [Huckleberry](https://huckleberrycare.com/): A sleep-tracking app with expert sleep guidance. It provides personalized sleep plans and recommendations for improving a baby’s rest.


Single Mothers

- Peanut: Builds connections with other single moms for support. It’s a great way to find companionship and advice from moms with similar experiences.

- [Hello Mamas](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hello-mamas-community/id6736908394): A platform for meeting and socializing with other single parents. It fosters friendships and provides a safe space for sharing parenting tips.


Working Mothers

- Todoist: Enhances productivity for managing work and home life. It helps balance professional responsibilities with parenting duties.

- Mint: Helps track budgets and expenses efficiently. With automated financial tracking, it simplifies managing household finances.


Mothers With a Disabled Child

- [Birdhouse for Autism](https://appadvice.com/app/birdhouse-for-autism/648397801): Helps parents track symptoms, treatments and therapies. It provides insights into behavioral patterns and medication schedules to support special needs care.

- [MyMedSchedule Plus](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.medactionplan.mymedscheduleplus&hl=en-US): Simplifies medication management with reminders, dosage tracking and refill alerts — ideal for parents managing complex treatment plans.

- [Insight Timer](https://insighttimer.com/): Offers guided meditations, breathing exercises and relaxation tools to help parents reduce stress and practice mindfulness while caring for their child.


Stay-At-Home Mothers

- [Tinybeans:](https://tinybeans.com/) A digital baby book to document memories. It allows parents to share photos and milestones with family in a private, ad-free space.

- [Mealime](https://www.mealime.com/): Provides easy, family-friendly meal planning. With customizable meal plans and grocery lists, it simplifies cooking for the whole family.


## How To Choose the Right App for You

With so many apps out there, it’s easy to get lost in the scroll. If you’re after a productivity booster, a parenting lifesaver or just a little fun, here’s how to pick the perfect one without the endless download-and-delete cycle!

- Purpose: Identify your specific need (organization, socializing, health, parenting, etc.) and select an app that aligns with it.

- User-Friendliness: Choose an app with an intuitive interface that makes navigation seamless.

- Customization: Look for apps that allow personalization to fit your unique parenting style.

- Security: Ensure your personal information is protected with encryption and privacy settings.

- Cost: Check if the app is free or requires a subscription and consider its value in relation to your budget.


## Tips for Integrating Apps Into Your Daily Routine

Using apps effectively can simplify your life, but it’s important to use them in a way that supports, rather than overwhelms, your day. Here’s how to make the most of them:

- Set Smart Reminders: Use apps to schedule alerts for feeding times, medical appointments, school events or even self-care breaks. Choose notifications that are helpful but not disruptive.

- Break Tasks Into Steps: Parenting can be overwhelming, so prioritize manageable goals. Apps with to-do lists or habit trackers can help break larger responsibilities into smaller, more achievable steps.

- Use Family Calendars: Sync schedules with partners, caregivers or older kids to keep everyone on the same page. Many apps allow shared access, making it easier to coordinate activities and appointments.

- Automate Where Possible: Take advantage of apps that offer automation, such as recurring reminders for medications, grocery delivery lists or bill payments, to reduce mental load.

- Customize App Features: Many apps allow for personalized settings — adjust notifications, layouts and data tracking to fit your lifestyle and preferences.

- Avoid Digital Overload: While apps can be helpful, too much screen time can lead to stress. Set specific times for checking apps and take breaks to stay present with your family.

- Evaluate Regularly: Every few months, review which apps are truly helpful. If an app feels like more of a hassle than a help, don’t be afraid to delete it and try a different one.


By using apps with intention, you can streamline daily responsibilities while maintaining a balanced and connected family life!
